title: Tick-level price velocity & headcount hedgebook
summary: Working notebook that maps sub-hour (tick-level) price swings to short-term headcount and capacity hedges. Prototype of operational playbook to protect margin during rapid price velocity events while preserving SLA for enterprise customers.
executive_summary: We observe increasing short-duration price volatility driven by spot GPU availability and heavy tail customer spikes. This document proposes a three-layer hedge: (1) Price gating windows (customer-tier micropricing) to throttle non-critical traffic during ticks, (2) short-term contractor pool and surge-staffing rotations to cover predictable burst windows, and (3) contract-level GPU mix toggles (spot vs reserved) automated by signal thresholds. Preliminary simulations show a 12-18% margin protection in high-volatility scenarios with a modest incremental monthly cost of ~3-5% in low-volatility periods.
assumptions:
- Baseline token unit economics from Feb 2026 model (token_cost_usd=0.0009 avg).
- Spot GPU price volatility: daily stdev 8%, intra-day spikes up to +45% observed in Q4 2025.
- Hiring lead time for contractors: 7 days to onboard vs full-time 45 days.
- Service-tier mix: 60% self-serve, 30% mid-market, 10% enterprise (enterprise has SLA exemption from aggressive gating).
- Ability to enforce per-route gating and soft-fallbacks via Console (engineering sprint in progress).
- Short bursts are correlated with specific customer cohorts (top 5 customers drive 22% of minute-level spikes).
headcount_plan:
Overview: Create a 3-bucket staffing hedge aligned to price-signal tiers.
Buckets: 1) Core FT ops (unchanged). 2) Reserve contractor pool (30 FTE-equivalent hours weekly across timezones). 3) Flexible internal on-call swap (voluntary stipend-based).
Phasing: Month 0-1: recruit contractor pool (pilot 10 people, 6-week rolling contracts). Month 2-4: evaluate engagement and convert 0-2 to FT if utilization >60%. Month 3: run tabletop with SRE and billing to validate gating behaviors.
Role mix and approximate cost multipliers (fully loaded monthly):
- SRE contractor (senior): $18k
- GPU ops contractor (junior): $9k
- On-call stipend pool (per head): $800/mo average
- Conversion budget runway: $120k reserved for potential FT hires over next 6 months.

sensitivity_analysis:
Approach: run 3 axis sensitivity (spot volatility magnitude, spike frequency, contractor utilization).
Key scenarios:
- Low-volatility / low-frequency: margin hit <1%, contractor utilization ~10% (pilot cost becomes pure overhead).
- Medium volatility (baseline): margin protection 12%, contractor utilization 45-55%.
- High volatility (40% intra-day spikes): margin protection 18-22% when all hedges active; contractor utilization >80% and conversion recommended.
Break-even calculus: with current pricing, gating that reduces non-enterprise traffic by 20% during ticks yields immediate margin restoration if contractor utilization >30%.
Role impact: SRE-heavy response is costlier but reduces SLA violation risk vs purely gating-first approach.
Graph notes (refer to simulation CSV linked): peak_margin_protection correlates non-linearly with spike amplitude; beyond +60% spike the only reliable protection is pre-provisioned reserved capacity.
recommended_actions:
1) Launch 6-week contractor pilot (budget approval request: $120k) to stand up the operational hedge.
2) Implement per-route soft gating and customer-tier override in Console (eng ticket backlog prioritization).
3) Add tick-level spot-price monitor to Optimize signals and wire to an automated toggle that flips reserve curtain at threshold.
4) Run weekly burn + utilization cadence for pilot and decide on conversion at week 5.
5) Communicate with top 10 customers about potential temporary soft-throttles and premium bypass during experiments.
6) Re-run payback model after first 30 days and present to CFO and Head of SRE.
open_questions: What is legal/contract exposure for gated reduction of non-critical traffic for mid-market customers?
Can Console implement sub-minute gating without impacting metrics labeling and billing?
How many of the top 25 customers are eligible for enterprise bypass vs subject to gating?
What is the realistic contractor sourcing lead time in APAC (we need timezone coverage)?
